name: Germ Cell Tumor

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in East Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (for intracranial GCTs)

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of germ cell tumor cells
Elevated serum or CSF tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
Characteristic radiological findings on MRI or CT consistent with germ cell tumor
Symptoms consistent with tumor location and mass effect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus either elevated tumor markers or characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may vary depending on tumor location (gonadal vs extragonadal).

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of non-seminomatous germ cell tumors
Common in choriocarcinoma and some seminomas

common.symptomName: Headache due to intracranial germ cell tumor
searchTerms: head pain due to brain tumor

common.notes: Due to hormone secretion by tumor

searchTerms: symptoms of fluid buildup in brain
nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vision problems from brain fluid buildup

occasional.notes: In pediatric patients with hormone-secreting tumors

occasional.symptomName: Back pain from spinal germ cell tumors
searchTerms: spine pain caused by tumor growth
pain in back due to spinal mass
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

rare.symptomName: Gynecological symptoms in females (e.g., ovarian mass)
searchTerms: female pelvic symptoms like ovarian lump

rare.notes: Due to mediastinal germ cell tumors

imaging: MRI showing mass lesions in gonads or intracranial sites
CT scan demonstrating mediastinal or retroperitoneal masses
Ultrasound of testes showing hypoechoic lesions
genetic: No specific germline mutations; some tumors show chromosomal abnormalities such as isochromosome 12p
other: Histopathological examination confirming germ cell tumor subtype
Tumor marker analysis in cerebrospinal fluid for intracranial tumors

distinguishingFeatures: Lymphoma often presents with systemic B symptoms
Lymph node biopsy shows lymphoid cells rather than germ cells
Tumor markers AFP and β-hCG are not elevated
Lack of germ cell tumor markers elevation
May not elevate AFP or β-hCG unless mixed with other germ cell components
Histology differentiates teratoma from other germ cell tumors

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging testicular or mediastinal mass
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (headache, vomiting, papilledema)
Elevated tumor markers AFP or β-hCG indicating malignant germ cell tumor
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Testicular Cancer, 2024
